name: Terminal Title Update On Every Message
description: Neutralizes the one-shot guard on Claude Code's auto-generated terminal title so the title regenerates on every qualifying user message instead of only the first. The title-generation block is gated by `!s1.current` and latches the guard via `s1.current=!0;` immediately after firing; flipping that success-path arm to `s1.current=!1;` (single byte 0x30->0x31) keeps the gate open so subsequent messages re-run title generation. Same-length single-byte swap. Mirrors the core mechanism of antonioacg/claude-code-title-patch (which performs `!0`->`!1` guard swaps); the upstream disk-persistence and resume-reader rewrites (sites 4-5) are inherently length-changing and are not part of this same-length binary edit.

provenance.author: antonioacg
provenance.derived_by: anchored against pristine 2.1.158 using 2.1.88 source ref

operations.rationale: The auto-title generation block is gated by `!s1.current` and immediately latches the one-shot guard with `s1.current=!0;` on the success path, so a title is produced only for the first message. Flipping `!0`->`!1` (one byte) prevents the latch from closing, keeping the gate open so the title regenerates on every qualifying message. Anchored on the globally-unique landmark `.message.content):null;if(...)){` which precedes the guard arm; backref \g<1> preserves churned minified identifiers (guard ref `s1`, content helper, predicate).
